scope: Independent pre-freeze review of new experience modules and offline evaluation runner
validation_command: conda run -n adaptive-rag python -m pytest tests/unit/test_experience_review.py -q --basetemp data/local/a6-review-scratch-01 --junitxml research/docs/agent_engineering_upgrade/p3_experience_shadow/evidence/a6_independent_review.xml
validation_result: 4 expected RED counterexamples, 1.35 seconds; no fixes applied by reviewer

findings.title: Delete does not atomically enforce the caller's expected version
findings.evidence: Synthetic AsyncSession hook commits an independent PROPOSED to NEEDS_REVIEW update immediately after delete reads version 1. delete(expected_version=1) nevertheless succeeds and deletes the version-2 record because ORM DELETE has no version predicate.
findings.required_behavior: Atomically condition deletion on ID, scope and expected_version; fail and roll back tombstone/event deletions if no row matches.

findings.title: Verification evidence references bypass provenance privacy checks
findings.evidence: A valid synthetic validation report named reviewer.person@example.com.json is accepted for VERIFIED_OFFLINE and its personal identifier is serialized directly into ExperienceEventRow.evidence_ref. Candidate provenance applies privacy checks, but governance provenance does not.
findings.required_behavior: Revalidate and apply the same bounded provenance privacy checks to verification artifact/pointer strings before resolving or persisting them.

findings.title: Malformed evidence pointers resolve as valid evidence
findings.evidence: The resolver accepts /-1 on a JSON list as its last element and accepts the invalid JSON Pointer escape /~2 as an object key. Python int indexing and unchecked escape replacement disagree with the promised fail-closed evidence-reference contract.
findings.required_behavior: Validate JSON Pointer escapes and canonical nonnegative list index syntax before traversal, rejecting negative, signed and leading-zero array indices and unsupported tilde escapes.

limits: Synthetic counterexamples establish the listed boundary failures only. They do not establish learning benefit, independent source truth, human calibration, live PostgreSQL behavior or production authentication. Offline identity assertions and hash-bound report metadata are accepted as the documented trusted-operator boundary.
